angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,269,648 km at 34.57 pc = 2.42 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: distance 34.566 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 34.566 +/- 0.242 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 28.7314 +/- 0.1583 mas (same row, RUWE 2.90), 181.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 9.012 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: radius 9.012 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 39.708 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,269,648 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4830 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: effective temperature 4830 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: effective temperature 4830 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * kap Per: spectral type G9.5IIIb (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * kap Per: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * kap Per: projected rotation speed 3 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 164) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.08 from 2016A&A...587A...2B; the 21 published values span log g 2.68 to 3.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016A%26A...587A...2B)
